summary:
All evidence gathered — tests verified green (23/23), packaging verified working, docs cross-checked, code traced. Report follows.

## Review — commit 8159042 (structure / simplicity / contract consistency)

**Verified good:** code tree matches `Code-Structure.md` "실제" sections exactly; namespaces obey CONVENTIONS (`Communication.Shared.*`, `Communication.Network.TCP`); `Public-API.md` signatures match `ISession`/`TcpConnector`/`IMessageConverter`/`IMessageHandler` verbatim; ownership boundary is clean (`Session.MarkDisconnected` disposes pipeline→channel; pipeline never disposes channel, documented); `AttachPipeline` once-only guard works; dual-mode `MessagePipeline` branching is confined to 2 ctors / `Start()` / two loop pairs — splitting would duplicate the queue/backpressure/dispatch core, so **no split needed**; 23/23 tests pass (`dotnet test`); `dotnet pack` works (`PackageReadmeFile` resolves via packed root README — suspected bug disproven). Test flakiness risk: **none found** (deterministic coalesce test, bounded `WaitUntilAsync` polls, port-0 loopback).

### Ranked findings

1. **MAJOR | `Source/Communication.Shared/Messages/MessagePipeline.cs:202-211, 247-251` | Flush tasks orphan forever when `Serialize` throws.** In `WriteCoalescedBatchAsync`, items are dequeued into `_batch`; if `_converter.Serialize` throws mid-batch, the flush-fault `catch` (line 225) only wraps `WriteAsync`, so `_batch` items' `Flush` TCSs are never completed — `DrainSendQueueFaulted` (line 442) only drains `_sendQueue`. Same shape in `SendLoopMessageAsync` (Serialize at 250, fault only at 259). `await SendAndFlushAsync` hangs indefinitely. *Fix:* wrap the dequeue/serialize loop so any exception faults `Flush` of every already-dequeued item before rethrowing.

2. **MAJOR | `MessagePipeline.cs:200-211` vs `Framing/LengthPrefixFramer.cs:14-21` | `MaxFrameLength` is never enforced on the real wire path.** The pipeline back-patches its own length header inline and never checks the ca...
